    AI Overview
    The Renaissance (c. 14th–16th centuries) was a fervent period of European cultural, artistic, political, and scientific "rebirth" following the Middle Ages, originating in Italy and spreading across Europe. It was characterized by the revival of Classical antiquity, humanism, and groundbreaking innovations in art, science, and exploration. 
    Key Aspects and Usage Examples 
    • Art and Architecture: Shifted toward realism, perspective, and human emotion, featuring artists like Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, and Raphael.
    • Intellectual Movement (Humanism): Focused on human potential and achievements, studying classical Greek and Roman texts
      .
    • Technology and Science: The invention of the printing press (c. 1440) revolutionized information sharing. The scientific method grew, challenging old Ptolemaic systems.
    • Culture: The term is used in phrases like "a renaissance of classical learning" or "a new artistic renaissance". 
    Synonyms and Related Terms 
    • Rebirth/Revival: Emphasizing the return to classical ideas.
    • Early Modern Period: The historical era covering the Renaissance.
    • Rinascita: The original Italian term used by Giorgio Vasari.
    • Renewal/Reawakening: Reflecting the cultural shift. 
    Key Figures and Centers 
    • Florence: The birthplace, heavily influenced by the Medici family.
    • Key Figures: Michelangelo, Leonardo da Vinci, Raphael, Machiavelli, Galileo. 
    The era saw the decline of the feudal system and the rise of commerce.
